From: Lena Park <lena@atlasai.com>

Subject: Activation orchestration & billing grace window — Redwood / AtlasAI

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. AtlasAI is ready to move forward on the AWS Marketplace SaaS listing, but we have one operational constraint we need to iron out before procurement will sign. Our billing system processes metering events in near-real time, however our partner gateway sometimes delivers usage webhooks with up to a 48-72 hour delay due to internal batching and retries.

If Marketplace metering is strictly enforced at event arrival time, we risk double-counting (replayed events) and sudden spikes for customers who switch plans mid-day. Procurement asked whether Redwood can support a short billing "grace window" (72 hours max) combined with idempotent deduplication keyed on entitlement_id + usage_window to avoid re-billing. Alternatively, they asked if we can guarantee activation orchestration that delays the Marketplace fulfillment acknowledgement until AtlasAI confirms entitlements (can be 24h).

Can you share an ops playbook for activation sequencing and a proposed SLA exception/acknowledgement flow we can send to our legal/procurement team? If there are alternate integration patterns you prefer (immediate webhook + dedupe v. delayed ack + batch), please outline pros/cons.

Attn: procurement@atlasai.com for context.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Head of Partnerships, AtlasAI

Thanks — reviewed the playbook. Two recommended integration options with details so we can present both to AtlasAI: 

Option 1 (recommended): Real-time ingestion with idempotent dedupe- AtlasAI sends usage events as they occur. Required fields: entitlement_id, customer_id (marketplace account id), usage_amount, usage_window_start, usage_window_end, event_id (UUID), timestamp, product_sku. Redwood will perform dedupe using (event_id) + (entitlement_id) and reject duplicates. This keeps billing accurate and low-latency.

Pros: low latency for customers, simpler for Redwood billing.
Cons: AtlasAI must guarantee reasonably unique event_id and stable entitlement_id mapping.

Option 2: Deferred fulfillment acknowledgement (grace window)- AtlasAI continues to batch internal processing and sends a daily/48h batch. Redwood will hold fulfillment ACK to AWS Marketplace for up to N hours (configurable; suggest 72h max) and perform a dedupe pass on arrival, using (entitlement_id + usage_window) as dedupe key. If AtlasAI cannot produce event_id, we'll rely on deterministic aggregation per window.

Telemetry hooks and minimal requirements for both patterns:
- A test webhook environment (staging) with sample payloads.
- A reconciliation endpoint where AtlasAI can POST a daily CSV of usage rows for cross-check.
- Error/retry webhook with a dead-letter for failed events.
- Versioned webhook schema; attach v2 below.

I attached webhook_schema_v2.json and a small entitlement_mapping.csv with expected fields. I can run a short integration spike with AtlasAI's eng team if they want.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Infra/Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
